title: Inside a decoder: from text to the next token
summary: Trace every tensor through a decoder transformer, calculate attention by hand, and defend the architectural choices behind autoregressive language models.
learningObjectives: Trace token IDs, hidden states, attention heads, and vocabulary logits with explicit shapes.
Calculate a masked attention row and a next-token distribution.
Explain position, normalization, residual paths, and gated MLPs without treating them as interchangeable.
Distinguish parallel teacher-forced training from sequential generation and reusable inference state.

sections.title: 1. The model's contract is conditional prediction
paragraphs: A decoder language model assigns a distribution to the next token given a prefix. A chat interface supplies that prefix by serializing messages, role delimiters, and any tool results into a model-specific template. The transformer does not receive an intrinsic JavaScript conversation object. Its input is a sequence of IDs, plus position and masking information. Getting this boundary right prevents a common interview mistake: attributing application behavior such as authorization or durable memory to the neural network itself.

Let B be batch size, T sequence length, d hidden width, and V vocabulary size. An input has shape B × T; embedding lookup produces B × T × d; a stack of L decoder blocks preserves that shape. A final vocabulary projection produces B × T × V logits. At inference, the last relevant position predicts the next token. A decoder-only stack normally omits the cross-attention to a separate encoder present in the original translation transformer. [The original architecture](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762v7) is therefore a foundation, not a literal specification of every chat model.

sections.title: 2. Tokenization is an architectural interface
paragraphs: A token is not necessarily a word. Subword tokenizers represent common strings compactly while decomposing less common strings into smaller units. Byte-pair encoding learns merge rules; the trained tokenizer applies those rules deterministically under its configuration. Byte-level representations and byte fallback are related ways to improve coverage, but neither should be assumed for an arbitrary vocabulary. The [subword paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.07909) motivates decomposing rare words; the [Tokenizers components documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/tokenizers/main/en/components) distinguishes normalization, pre-tokenization, the tokenization model, and post-processing.

This interface has practical consequences. A change in whitespace, Unicode normalization, or a role delimiter can change the token sequence. Code, identifiers, and different languages can require very different token counts for visually similar amounts of text. A context limit applies to tokens, so character-count budgeting is only an estimate. Version the tokenizer and chat template with the checkpoint. Debugging a sudden quality regression should begin by inspecting the actual IDs and template, not immediately retraining weights.

The embedding table E has V rows and d columns. Token ID 17 selects row 17; it is not the scalar number 17 multiplied by a vector. For a hypothetical V=50,000 and d=4,096, the table contains 204,800,000 parameters, or 409,600,000 bytes in two-byte storage, approximately 390.6 MiB. That excludes gradients, optimizer state, and runtime buffers. If input and output embeddings are tied, the same parameter matrix also participates in the vocabulary projection; otherwise the output matrix adds a similarly sized parameter allocation.

sections.title: 3. Attention routes information between positions
paragraphs: For one attention head, learned projections map hidden states to queries Q, keys K, and values Vh. Queries and keys determine compatibility; values supply the vectors that are mixed. With head dimension dₕ, Q and K have shape T × dₕ for one sequence. Their product creates T × T scores. Softmax acts across permitted source positions separately for each query. In causal attention, position i can use positions j≤i; later positions receive a negative-infinity mask before softmax. See [scaled dot-product attention](https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762v7).

Calculate one row explicitly. Suppose a query has three permitted scaled scores [2,1,0], and the three value vectors are [1,0], [0,2], and [2,2]. Subtracting the maximum gives exponentials [1,0.3679,0.1353]; dividing by their sum gives weights approximately [0.6652,0.2447,0.0900]. The output is therefore [0.8453,0.6695]. A fourth, future position gets zero probability regardless of its unmasked score. This is a weighted mixture of learned vectors, not a lookup that copies the most likely source token.

Multiple heads learn different projections and mix their outputs through an output projection. With d=4,096 and 32 equal query heads, each head has width 128. Under the simplifying assumption that independent query/key components have zero mean and unit variance, an unscaled dot product has variance 128. Dividing by √128 restores variance near one, helping avoid immediate softmax saturation. Real trained activations need not satisfy those assumptions exactly; the derivation explains the scale factor rather than proving every model is normalized.
sections.formula: Attention(Q,K,Vh) = softmax(QKᵀ / √dₕ + M)Vh; Mᵢⱼ = 0 if j≤i, otherwise −∞

sections.title: 4. Position supplies order, not unlimited context
paragraphs: A content-only attention score cannot directly distinguish otherwise identical tokens at different locations. Position representations supply that missing information. Learned absolute embeddings add a position-dependent vector; sinusoidal embeddings add deterministic frequencies. Rotary position embedding instead rotates pairs of query and key coordinates as a function of position. The resulting dot product incorporates relative displacement. [RoFormer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09864) derives this property; it does not establish that arbitrary context lengths will work equally well.

Consider a two-dimensional pair initially [1,0]. Rotating it by 0 radians gives [1,0], and by π/2 gives [0,1]. Their dot product changes from one for matching angles to zero at that offset. Real RoPE applies multiple frequencies across coordinate pairs. This small construction explains the mechanism without implying tokens literally occupy a physical circle. A longer configured context changes the positions and dependencies encountered by the model; quality still depends on training, scaling choices, and evaluation. Test retrieval at different depths and distractor densities before promising long-context reliability.

sections.title: 5. Residuals, normalization, and MLPs do different jobs
paragraphs: In a typical pre-normalized block, attention reads a normalized residual stream and adds an update back to the original stream. The MLP does the same in a second sublayer. The residual path gives features and gradients a route that does not require every sublayer to reconstruct the entire representation. Normalization controls activation scale; it does not store a conversation or normalize over the vocabulary. The [LLaMA paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2302.13971v1) describes a concrete decoder using pre-normalization, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, and rotary embeddings.

LayerNorm centers a token's feature vector and scales by its standard deviation, with learned affine parameters. RMSNorm rescales using root mean square without subtracting the feature mean. For x=[3,4], ignoring epsilon and using unit gain, RMS=√12.5≈3.5355, so RMSNorm returns approximately [0.8485,1.1314]. LayerNorm on the same vector, under the same simplifying assumptions, returns [-1,1]. This calculated difference shows why replacing one with the other changes the function. [RMSNorm](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07467) motivates dropping the centering step.

Attention mixes positions; a standard dense MLP transforms features independently at each position using shared weights. A SwiGLU MLP multiplies a SiLU-activated projection by a second projection, then projects back to d. The gate is continuous, not a discrete expert router. Its three matrices require approximately 3dm parameters when the intermediate width is m, compared with 2dm for a two-matrix MLP of that same width. Match parameter budgets before attributing an improvement entirely to activation choice. [GLU variants](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.05202) provide the experimental motivation for gated feed-forward layers.
sections.formula: u = x + Attention(Norm(x)); y = u + MLP(Norm(u)); SwiGLU(x) = [SiLU(xWg) ⊙ (xWu)]Wd

sections.title: 6. Logits become decisions through a decoding policy
paragraphs: The final hidden state is projected to V logits, real-valued scores with no requirement to sum to one. Softmax converts these to probabilities. For logits [2,1,0] and temperature τ=1, probabilities are [0.6652,0.2447,0.0900]. At τ=0.5, the scaled logits [4,2,0] produce approximately [0.8668,0.1173,0.0159]. Temperature changes concentration without changing rank for positive τ. It does not add knowledge, correct a false premise, or calibrate factual confidence.

Greedy decoding selects the highest-scoring next token. Sampling draws from a distribution, often after top-k or nucleus filtering. With the first distribution above, nucleus threshold 0.9 retains the first two tokens because their cumulative mass is approximately 0.9099, then renormalizes them. Greedy decisions need not maximize the probability of the entire completed sequence. Stop tokens, maximum output length, repetition controls, and structured-output constraints are additional policy choices. The [generation guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/generation_strategies) separates these methods; save their configuration with an experiment so comparisons are reproducible.
sections.formula: pᵢ = exp((zᵢ − max(z))/τ) / Σⱼ exp((zⱼ − max(z))/τ), for τ>0

sections.title: 7. Parallel training and sequential inference share one model
paragraphs: During teacher-forced training, the full observed sequence is available. Inputs [A,B,C] can predict targets [B,C,D] in one masked forward pass; each position remains forbidden from seeing its future target. Average negative log probability of the targets gives cross-entropy. If target probabilities are 0.5, 0.25, and 0.125, mean loss is about 1.3863 nats and perplexity is exp(loss)=4. These are calculated values for an invented sequence. A suspiciously low loss can signal a missing causal mask or incorrectly shifted labels rather than an excellent model.

Generation cannot know the next sampled ID in advance. It processes the prefix, chooses a token, appends it, and repeats. In causal inference, prior positions do not change when later tokens are appended, so each layer can reuse their projected keys and values. The new query still attends over those cached positions. [Hugging Face's cache explanation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/cache_explanation) describes this reuse. A KV cache is model execution state tied to an exact prefix and model configuration; it is not a durable conversation database or a cache of finished answers.

For ordinary multi-head attention, a cache estimate is 2 × L × B × T × Hkv × dₕ × bytes_per_element. With 32 layers, one sequence, 4,096 cached tokens, 32 KV heads, head width 128, and two-byte elements, that is 2,147,483,648 bytes, or 2 GiB, excluding allocator overhead. This original sizing example makes the architectural stakes tangible: reducing KV heads changes memory, whereas merely lowering sampling temperature does not. Use exact checkpoint dimensions when planning capacity.

interview.question: A teammate says doubling the context window is harmless because the model has unchanged parameter count, and a KV cache makes generation constant-time. How do you respond?
interview.answer: Separate weights from runtime state. For dense causal attention, doubling prefix length roughly quadruples the pairwise attention work during prefill, while projection and MLP work grow linearly in token count. The KV cache grows linearly with cached tokens. Each ordinary decode query must still read and attend across its relevant cached prefix, so cache reuse removes recomputation of prior keys and values without making context-independent latency. Kernel behavior, memory bandwidth, batching, and attention variants affect observed scaling. I would calculate KV bytes using the checkpoint's KV head count, measure time to first token and per-token latency at representative lengths, and evaluate answer quality at long positions rather than assuming a configured limit guarantees useful recall.
followUps: What changes if the model uses grouped-query attention?
How would a broken padding mask differ from a broken causal mask?
Which cached entries remain valid when a user edits an earlier message?

pitfalls: Treating token IDs as ordered numeric features instead of lookup indices.
Confusing attention weights over positions with vocabulary probabilities over next tokens.
Applying causal masking after softmax without correct renormalization.
Assuming every decoder reproduces the original encoder-decoder paper exactly.
Using low temperature as a substitute for factual validation.
Reusing a KV cache after changing its prefix, model, or position interpretation.
checklist: Write B, T, d, V, head count, and head width before reasoning about tensors.
Inspect tokenizer version, special tokens, and the complete chat template.
Check shifted targets, causal masking, padding behavior, and loss masking separately.
State normalization placement and the actual MLP variant.
Calculate weight memory and KV memory as separate allocations.
Record decoding settings and evaluate quality alongside latency.

flashcards.front: What does a decoder language model directly predict?
flashcards.back: A next-token distribution conditioned on a token prefix. Conversation roles and tools enter through serialization; the model does not intrinsically manage application state.

flashcards.front: What are the input, hidden-state, and logit shapes?
flashcards.back: B × T IDs become B × T × d hidden states and B × T × V logits. The last valid position supplies next-token logits during generation.

flashcards.front: Why can equal-length strings consume different context budgets?
flashcards.back: A tokenizer segments using its learned vocabulary and preprocessing. Characters, words, and tokens are different units, especially across languages and code.

flashcards.front: How much storage does a 50,000 × 4,096 embedding table require at two bytes per parameter?
flashcards.back: 204.8 million parameters occupy 409.6 million bytes, about 390.6 MiB, excluding gradients and other state. Tying the output projection can avoid a second matrix.

flashcards.front: Why are keys and values separate?
flashcards.back: Keys participate in compatibility scores with queries; values are the information vectors mixed using those scores. Separate projections allow routing and payload to differ.
Under independent unit-variance components, dot-product variance grows as dₕ. Scaling controls that growth and reduces softmax saturation; the assumptions are an explanatory approximation.

flashcards.front: Where does the causal mask enter?
flashcards.back: Before softmax, forbidden source scores become negative infinity so they receive zero probability. This prevents future-target leakage while training many positions together.

flashcards.front: What does RoPE rotate, and what does it not guarantee?
flashcards.back: It rotates query/key coordinate pairs by position-dependent angles, producing relative-position effects in their dot products. It does not guarantee useful behavior at arbitrary context lengths.

flashcards.front: What distinguishes residual connections from normalization?
flashcards.back: Residual additions preserve a direct stream and gradient route while sublayers add updates. Normalization controls feature scale; the two solve different problems.

flashcards.front: How does RMSNorm differ from LayerNorm?
flashcards.back: RMSNorm rescales using root mean square without subtracting the feature mean. LayerNorm centers and rescales, so swapping them changes the network function.

flashcards.front: Does a standard transformer MLP mix token positions?
flashcards.back: No. It applies shared feature transformations independently at each position. Attention supplies cross-position mixing; gated MLPs modulate features with continuous products.

flashcards.front: What does lowering positive temperature change?
flashcards.back: It sharpens the next-token probability distribution without changing logit ordering. This changes sampling behavior, not the model's knowledge or factual calibration.

flashcards.front: Why can training predict multiple positions at once but ordinary generation cannot?
flashcards.back: Teacher forcing supplies the observed prefix at every training position, with causal masking. At inference, each chosen next token is needed before the following conditional distribution can be evaluated.

flashcards.front: What does a KV cache save, and what work remains?
flashcards.back: It stores prior projected keys and values per layer. New tokens avoid recomputing that state but must still compute their own states and attend over applicable cached positions.
